title: Signals by Police, Officials & Other Drivers
whatItIs: Signals from the police, other officials and other road users tell you what they are about to do, or what you must do.

keyFacts.text: You MUST obey signals from the police, traffic officers and school crossing patrols.
If the police signal you to stop (blue lights, headlights, left indicator), you MUST pull over and stop when safe.

keyFacts: Flashing headlights should only mean 'I'm here'. Never treat it as a signal to go.

keyFacts.text: You MUST NOT use your horn while stationary, or between 11.30 pm and 7 am in a built-up area, unless there is danger.

keyFacts: Hazard lights: when stopped and blocking traffic, or briefly on a motorway or dual carriageway to warn of danger ahead.

items.title: Arm signals (right arm)
items.text: Straight out: turning right. Circling: turning left. Moving up and down: slowing down.

items.title: Police asking you to stop
items.text: Headlights flashing, indicator on and pointing left. Pull over safely.

items.title: Flashing headlights
items.text: Only means 'I'm here'. Make your own decision.

items.title: Horn
items.text: Only to warn others you're there, and only while moving.

items.title: Hazard warning lights
items.text: When stopped and causing an obstruction. Never as an excuse to park.

items.title: School crossing patrol
items.text: When the patrol shows the 'Stop' sign, you MUST stop.

b.label: Police signal to stop
points: Pull over as soon as it's safe

onTheTest.question: Another driver flashes their headlights at you at a junction. What should you do?
options: Make your own decision about when it is safe
onTheTest.why: Flashing headlights should only mean 'I'm here'. Don't take it as an invitation: check for yourself that it's safe.

traps: Flashing headlights is not a signal to go.
Arm signals are given with the right arm: circling it means you are turning left.
Hazard lights don't make it OK to park where you shouldn't.
